subject: Prod latency/429s — NovaCredit (reserved pool saturation)
messages:
From: Claire Jacobs <claire.jacobs@novacredit.com>

Cc: ops@novacredit.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency spikes + 429s — urgent

Hi Kimberly,

We're seeing a sustained spike in generation latency and a rising rate of 429s against our reserved capacity since ~08:40 PT. Impact: our customer-facing user flows are timing out, and the support queue is getting filled with 'request timeout' and 'rate limit' errors. Sample metrics attached (novacredit_logs_20270624.tar.gz).

Quick summary from our side:
- 95th latency jumped from ~350ms to ~1.6s since 08:40
- 429s now ~3% of requests, concentrated on the /v1/generate route
- Throughput appears constrained even though our reserved pool shows green in the Console

Can Redwood confirm whether this is a runtime-side backlog or something on our integration? We're on the dedicated/reserved plan (NOVA-ENT-0423). This is customer-impacting for our lending decisioning flows.

We need a patch/ETA ASAP. We're standing by for a bridge.

Thanks,
Claire Jacobs
Sr. Eng Manager, Production
NovaCredit

On Fri, Jun 25, 2027 at 9:28 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Claire — thanks for the quick heads up and logs. We've triaged on our side and are escalating now.

Quick technical summary from infra:
- Observed behavior: dedicated/reserved pool for NovaCredit (pool id: NOVA-RSV-11) shows sustained GPU utilization at 98% across backends starting 08:36 PT. Queue depth increased sharply leading to internal request timeouts and 429 responses from the balancer.
- Metrics snapshot (08:40-09:40 PT):
  - inbound RPS: +32% vs 24h baseline
  - avg serve time (small model): 210ms -> 480ms
  - 95th latency (generation): 350ms -> 1.6s
  - 429 rate: 0.1% -> 3.2%
  - reserved-pool utilization: 98% (no available headroom in autoscale policy)

Root cause hypothesis: workload spike combined with request-size skew (longer contexts + multimodal traces) exhausted the reserved capacity. The autoscale policy for this reserved pool is conservative (scale by 1 node after 10m sustained pressure).

Short-term mitigations (can execute now if approved):
1) Route a subset of traffic to a smaller model variant (quantized) to reduce per-token compute. Expected latency reduction ~25–40%.
2) Temporarily increase reserved capacity via burst allocation (requires infra approval — takes ~15–30m to spin up GPUs).
3) Apply aggressive batching and KV-cache reuse for repeat prefixes (requires SDK flag change on customer side or Redwood edge config).

I've attached a csv with the metrics window (pool_metrics_0900-0940.csv). Recommend approval for 2) + 1) in that order. If we go to burst, we should also schedule a canary release to verify correctness.

I'll be on the bridge.

— Aditya Rao
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: pool_metrics_0900-0940.csv (metrics export)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: NovaCredit reserved throughput breach — exec bridge request

Marissa / Aditya — summary and ask:
- NovaCredit (NOVA-ENT-0423) is experiencing a reserved-capacity saturation that is producing customer-facing 429s and 95th latency regressions. Infra confirms reserved-pool utilization at ~98% and autoscale policy delay prevents immediate headroom.
- Proposed emergency actions:
  1) Approve immediate burst allocation for up to 2 additional GPU nodes (expected spin-up 15–30m).
  2) Offer NovaCredit a one-week operational credit for impacted hours and commit to a follow-up remediation plan (model/quantization roadmap + autoscale policy adjustment).
  3) Legal/Finance standby for contract amendment if NovaCredit requests a permanent capacity increase.

Please confirm approval for 1) so Aditya can trigger infra. If approved, I'll send an exec note to NovaCredit and get Legal looped in. I've attached a proposed SLA exception draft for your review.

Suggested customer-facing language (short):
"We apologize for the impact. Redwood has authorized a temporary capacity burst and a service credit for impacted hours while we implement a durable mitigation. We will follow up with a remediation timeline by EOD"

— Kimberly
